questions.question: Why can't 'pause for approval' just be input() in the agent's process?
options: The approver may answer hours later, and the process may restart or be one of many workers
questions.explanation: Pausing has to mean saving the state and stopping, so any process can resume later.

questions.question: Why does Checkpointer.save write a temp file and then call os.replace?
options: os.replace is atomic: readers see the old or the new checkpoint, never a half-written one
questions.explanation: A crash mid-write would otherwise leave a corrupt checkpoint and an unresumable run.

questions.question: After a crash, how does advance() know which tool calls still need to run?
options: It keeps a counter in memory
It finds tool calls in the latest assistant message that have no matching tool result in the history
questions.explanation: The history is the source of truth. Calls with results are done; the rest aren't.

questions.question: A human rejects a refund with the reason 'refund only half'. What does the model see?
options: An error observation with the reason, telling it not to retry the call as-is
questions.explanation: Rejections are observations, so the model can adapt (refund half) instead of the run dying.

questions.question: The scripted test model picks its reply by counting assistant messages in the history. Why not use an iterator?
options: An iterator's position lives in the process; after a resume in a new process, it would start over
questions.explanation: Everything about a run must be recoverable from the saved state, including a fake model's position.

questions.question: A run crashes after the first of two tool calls in one turn. The first was a payment. What prevents a double charge on resume?
options: The payment's tool result was checkpointed before the crash, so resume sees it as done and runs only the second call
questions.explanation: Checkpointing after every tool result is what makes resume skip completed side effects. The in-flight call is the case for idempotency keys (Lesson 6).
